name: Monitor dependency bug reports and alert on critical issues with Apify, OpenAI, Google Sheets and Slack

parameters.content:
## Get alerts on risky bugs in the libraries you depend on

### How it works
1. Runs by hand, or every weekday at 9:00 once you publish the workflow.
2. Fetches open issues updated in the last 7 days from each repository in node 1 with the [FetchCat GitHub Issues & Pull Requests Scraper](https://apify.com/fetch_cat/github-issues-pull-requests-scraper). No GitHub login needed.
3. Skips issues already in your sheet with no update since.
4. One OpenAI call scores each issue: category, upgrade or production risk from 1 to 5, whether it affects upgrades, and a one-line summary.
5. Logs every scored issue to Google Sheets (matched on url). Issues at risk 4 or higher go to one Slack digest, once each. A quiet day posts nothing.

### Setup (about 10 minutes)
- [ ] Make a copy of the [sheet template](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11lRVyqoPUyILjMfo0_Ni3iZh7hMt2211nj9TgB4_JPk/copy).
- [ ] Install the Apify node (verified node on n8n Cloud, `@apify/n8n-nodes-apify` on self-hosted) and connect your Apify account in node 2.
- [ ] Connect OpenAI in node 3.
- [ ] Connect Google Sheets in **Read Logged Issues** and node 4 and pick your copy.
- [ ] Connect Slack in node 5 and pick a channel.
- [ ] List your dependencies in node 1, then run once by hand.

### Cost
A default run (3 repositories, up to 10 issues each) costs about $0.02 on Apify plus one small gpt-5.4-mini call. `maxCostUsdPerRepository` caps each Apify run.

### Good to know
Scores rest on the title, labels, counts and the first 1,000 characters of each issue, not the full thread.

## Start
Run by hand to test. The weekday 9:00 schedule only runs after you publish the workflow.

## Your settings
Edit only node 1: repositories, lookback window, limits, the alert threshold and the Apify cost cap. The next node checks them before any paid request.

## Fetch issues
Runs the FetchCat GitHub issues Actor once per repository. A failed repository is reported and the others continue; if all fail, the run stops here.

## Pick new or updated
Issues already in your sheet with the same updatedAt are skipped, so unchanged issues are never scored twice.

## AI risk score
One gpt-5.4-mini call scores all picked issues. The answer is checked first; a bad answer writes nothing.

## Log to Google Sheets
Every scored issue is added or updated in the Dependency Issues tab, matched on url.

## Slack alert
Issues at or above alertMinRiskScore that were never alerted go into one digest. A quiet day posts nothing.

values.content:
=Issues from libraries this team depends on (JSON):
{{ JSON.stringify($json.issues.map(i => ({ ref: i.ref, repository: i.repository, type: i.type, title: i.title, labels: i.labels, commentsCount: i.commentsCount, reactions: i.reactions, createdAt: i.createdAt, bodyExcerpt: i.bodyExcerpt }))) }}

options.instructions: You triage GitHub issues and pull requests from open-source libraries that a product team depends on. For every item return one score with its ref copied exactly. category: bug, regression (something that used to work broke in a newer version), security, breaking-change, feature or question. riskScore from 1 to 5 for a team using this library in production or about to upgrade: 5 = confirmed security problem, data loss or a crash or regression in common use in a released version; 4 = likely to break typical users or block an upgrade; 3 = real bug with a narrow trigger or a workaround; 2 = minor bug, docs or edge case; 1 = feature request, question or no user impact. Many comments and reactions mean more people are affected. affectsUpgrade: yes only when the text ties the problem to a specific newer version or a change in behaviour between versions. summary: one plain sentence of at most 25 words on what breaks and for whom. Use only the supplied text; the body is an excerpt, so do not invent versions or facts.
